takeaway: Hot, sunny and dry, and it is turning windy. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has few clouds on the North Pacific all day today, Nicoya near 35°C, and no meaningful rain outside the mountains. For surf, the Caribbean trade winds are already back (offshore at Nosara) and the marine forecast is now stronger and earlier than yesterday: firm offshore today and Monday, then strong offshore Monday night through Friday. Expect clean mornings all week, with Tuesday to Thursday possibly blustery. No rainy spell and no tropical storm threat for the next two weeks.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Sun Nov 15 – Tue Nov 17)
periods.pattern: Dry air settles in. IMN says the Caribbean trade winds are still on the weak side today, which lets a little Pacific moisture in and keeps it muggy, but the afternoon storms stay in the Central and South Pacific mountains and around the Central Valley. The North Pacific stays mostly clear with occasional gusts in the hills. Trades firm up Monday and turn strong Tuesday. All three ensemble averages (American, European and the European AI model) keep rain near Nicoya very light; the heavy rain in the models sits on the Caribbean coast of Honduras and Nicaragua, not here.
periods.implications: Easy outdoor days. Hot afternoons, 34–35°C, still a bit humid today, then drier and breezier. Rain in Nosara is unlikely. Tuesday afternoon gets gusty.
periods.confidence: High on dry. Moderate on how fast the wind ramps up Tuesday.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Wed Nov 18 – Sat Nov 21)
periods.pattern: High pressure over the Caribbean drives a strong northeast wind across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica out over the Pacific. The marine forecast now calls for fresh to occasionally near-gale winds in the Gulf of Papagayo from Tuesday through Friday. IMN's weekly outlook has strong gusts in Guanacaste Tuesday and Wednesday, rain pushed to Limón, the Northern Zone and the eastern Central Valley, and fewer showers on the Pacific side. All three ensemble averages show the wind surge peaking Wednesday into Thursday.
periods.implications: Sunny, windy, dusty and dry. Rough water for boats, fishing trips and paddling offshore. Secure loose things outdoors and watch fire risk with dry brush. Nosara rain chances are very low.
periods.confidence: High on dry and windy. Moderate on the exact peak day and how long it lasts into Friday.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Sun Nov 22 – Sun Nov 29)
periods.pattern: Dry season settling in for good. The ensemble averages keep steady east to northeast trades through month's end, a bit less intense than midweek, with only light scattered rain near Nicoya. IMN's sub-seasonal outlook (Nov 16–Dec 13) says the dry season is established on the North Pacific with a below-normal rain pattern: roughly 0–65 mm for the whole week of Nov 16–22 and 0–50 mm for Nov 23–29 across the North Pacific region, low chance of any extreme event, and very low forecast uncertainty. The global tropics outlook is still dominated by El Niño and flags nothing near Central America.
periods.implications: Plan freely. Sunny, breezy days and hot afternoons. Rain gear not needed in Nosara for most of this stretch.
periods.confidence: High on dry overall. Low on any single day's wind strength.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trade winds (east to northeast), meaning offshore at Nosara, all week. Firm today and Monday, strong Monday night through Friday. This clearly favors offshore over Pacific onshore.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued about 3:30 a.m. Costa Rica time) has northeast to east winds of 15–20 knots in the Gulf of Papagayo and 10–15 knots elsewhere today, 15–20 knots Monday, then 20–25 knots Monday night through Thursday night, with near-gale gusts possible Tuesday to Friday. That is stronger and a day earlier than yesterday's forecast. Just south of the peninsula winds stay light and variable, so the trade wind is coming across the land, not along the coast. Swell: open-ocean seas of 3–5 ft from the southwest at 13–14 seconds most of the week (open-ocean numbers, not beach surf heights). Nicaragua should be offshore all day Tuesday to Friday, which points to strong Nosara mornings, but Nosara is not necessarily offshore all day: the afternoon sea breeze can still turn it side-on. With winds this strong, expect some blustery, wind-blown spray and harder paddling Tuesday to Thursday, and waves can be held up a bit.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Today and Monday: dawn to late morning, clean offshore; watch for a softer side-on sea breeze in the afternoon. Tuesday to Friday: dawn through late morning is the call; offshore may hold into the afternoon, but strong gusts can make it ragged, so earlier is better. Weekend of Nov 21–22: still offshore mornings, likely a touch less wind.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore all week. Moderate on how strong it gets at the beach versus out in the Gulf, and on afternoon sea-breeze timing.

gyreWatch.status: Not established. No watch needed. No prolonged rainy spell expected.
gyreWatch.supporting: Very little: today's weak trades let some Pacific moisture in, and the marine forecast mentions scattered showers offshore, mostly south and east of the peninsula.
gyreWatch.conflicting: Strong evidence against: firm to strong northeast trades all week (dry, offshore flow that pushes rain to the Caribbean side), all three ensemble averages light near Nicoya through Nov 27, the hurricane center expecting no tropical storm formation in the next 7 days, IMN's sub-seasonal outlook calling the dry season established with a low chance of extreme events, and a global tropics outlook with nothing near Central America.

whatChanged: The wind is coming in stronger and sooner. Yesterday's marine forecast had light trades today and the strong push starting Monday night at 15–20 knots; today it has firm offshore already today, 20–25 knots from Monday night, and near-gale gusts in Papagayo possible through Friday. The swell number dropped slightly to 3–5 ft from the southwest. IMN's sub-seasonal outlook now rates its forecast uncertainty as very low. The rain outlook is unchanged: dry.
practical: Surf early every day this week; dawn to late morning is the best window, and Tuesday to Thursday can get blustery. Stay hydrated in 34–35°C afternoons. Expect gusty, dusty afternoons from Tuesday; tie down umbrellas and loose gear, and be careful with any fire. Skip offshore boat or paddle trips Tuesday to Friday. No rain plans needed.
alerts: No active IMN warnings for Guanacaste (last notice Nov 13 was about short heavy downpours in the Central Valley and Caribbean mountains).
Marine: fresh to near-gale northeast winds in the Gulf of Papagayo Tuesday to Friday; rough water offshore.
